original_title: Metal Polyphenol Network Enables Photo‐ATRP Under Blue Light
title: Swapping copper for iron in photo-ATRP, no petrochemical ligands needed
blurb: A metal-polyphenol network built from 4-hydroxychalcone and FeBr3 runs photo-ATRP under 420 nm light instead of the usual copper/petro-ligand combo. Conversion tops out at 67.4% and dispersity gets down to 1.3, decent control but not exactly living up to the ATRP name.

original_title: Metal‐Free Basic Guanidinium Ionic Liquid as Dual Catalyst/Solvent for Room‐Temperature Epoxide Aminolysis to Access β‐Amino Alcohols
title: One ionic liquid, no metal, plays both catalyst and solvent
blurb: A basic guanidinium ionic liquid, [HTMG+][TFE-], opens epoxides with aromatic amines at room temperature while doubling as the reaction medium. Metal-free route to beta-amino alcohols, a scaffold that shows up everywhere from drugs to chiral catalysts, so a milder way in is worth having.

original_title: Direct and Reversible Esterification of a Phosphonic Acid under Ambient Conditions through a Dissociative Mechanism
title: A phosphonic acid that esterifies itself just by sitting in alcohol
blurb: 1-dimethylaminonaphthyl-8-phosphonic acid condenses spontaneously with alcohols to give monoesters at room temperature, something ordinary phosphonic acids simply don't do. The reaction is selective and reversible, and the evidence points to a dissociative mechanism that's off-limits to typical phosphonic acids.

original_title: Spin Crossover‐Mediated Low‐Energy Charge Transfer Excited States in a Heterogeneous Cobalt Photocatalyst
title: Getting LMCT chemistry to work in visible light without the ligands falling off
blurb: Ligand-to-metal charge transfer states are usually a UV-only trick, since pushing them into the visible with strongly donating ligands tends to just decompose the complex. Here the chemistry gets moved onto a heterogeneous single-atom cobalt catalyst instead, using spin crossover to reach low-energy charge-transfer states without wrecking the structure.

original_title: Silane, Germane, and Stannane Activation by an Iron Dinitrogen Compound to Access Dimetallotetrylides
title: An iron dinitrogen dimer tears silane, germane, and stannane apart
blurb: Feeding SiH4, GeH4, and SnH4 to an iron dinitrogen dimer strips every hydride off, building diirontetrylide cores bridged by bare Si, Ge, or Sn. The silicide comes out linear (Fe2Si), the germanide and stannanide bent, all confirmed by X-ray. One ligand scaffold, the whole group 14 hydride series activated.

original_title: Programming Iron Nuclearity and Coordination for Hydride‐Mediated Nitroarene Reduction
title: Dialing iron catalysts from lone atoms up to clusters, on purpose
blurb: Atomically defined iron-oxo clusters serve as precursors that, through controlled ligand removal, land on N-doped carbon as Fe sites ranging from isolated atoms to size-defined multinuclear clusters. That nuclearity control then tunes hydride-mediated nitroarene reduction, the kind of structure-to-activity handle few-atom cluster catalysis has mostly lacked.

original_title: The Natural Product Esculetin as an Efficient Photoacid for the Visible‐Light‐Mediated Acetalization/Ketalization Reaction
title: A plant coumarin doing photoacid duty for acetal synthesis
blurb: Esculetin, a coumarin that just sits around in plants, turns out to be an efficient photoacid under 427 nm light, catalyzing acetalization and ketalization at low loading. Aldehydes and alcohols go to acetals in high yield, and it handles some industrially relevant ketals too, a green catalyst that didn't need inventing, just noticing.

original_title: Molecular Engineering of N–H-Type ESIPT Fluorophores Enabling Tunable Emission and ESIPT-AIE Integration
title: Two independent dials on one ESIPT dye: color and whether it glows as a solid
blurb: Benzothiazole ESIPT fluorophores get two separate handles: swapping the para substituent tunes emission color continuously within normal ESIPT behavior, while acylating the N-H site instead pushes the molecule into ESIPT-AIE territory, big Stokes shifts and bright solid-state fluorescence. The two sites turn out to control genuinely different properties rather than just remixing the same effect.

original_title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Azidation of Benzylic C–H Bonds
title: A cobalt catalyst turns benzylic C-H bonds straight into azides
blurb: Direct benzylic C-H azidation using a commercially available cobalt/N,N-ligand system, with the C-H substrate as the limiting reagent rather than the azide source. Broad scope and decent functional-group tolerance, and early mechanistic work points toward a hydrogen-atom transfer step, standard territory for this chemistry but a genuinely useful shortcut to benzylic azides.

original_title: Nonequilibrium Navigation of a Rugged Energy Landscape Enables the Formation of Face-On Single-Domain Dodecagonal Quasicrystals
title: Catching a quasicrystal mid-decision about which crystal to become
blurb: Time-resolved SAXS on a self-assembling dendrimer shows a dodecagonal quasicrystal sitting as a metastable junction that then splits down two different kinetic paths: a deformation route to the A15 Frank-Kasper phase at lower temperature, or a slower mass-exchange route to whatever phase is actually thermodynamically favored. The quasicrystal isn't the endpoint here, it's the junction the system passes through on the way to something else.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Reprogramming Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks via Asymmetric Single-Atom Catalysts
title: Swap one nitrogen for oxygen and water at the electrode falls in line
blurb: A fast Joule-heating trick turns symmetric Co-N4 single-atom sites into lopsided Co-N3O1 sites, and that asymmetry reorganizes the hydrogen-bond network of interfacial water during electrocatalysis. The claim is that the metal site itself is steering how water arranges nearby, not just reacting in it, backed by characterization plus theory.

original_title: Insertion of CS2 into Bi–N Bonds: Coordination Chemistry and Reactivity of Bismuth Dithiocarbamates
title: CS2 wedges itself into bismuth-amide bonds
blurb: Halo(bismuth)amides react with CS2 to insert cleanly into the Bi-N bond, giving both known and new bismuth dithiocarbamates. Thrown at a CAAC carbene, these turn out less redox-active than plain bismuth halides, so the amide scaffold is quietly damping the chemistry everyone associates with bismuth.

original_title: Abundance is not survival: intratumoural immune-cell fate as a missing endpoint in antibody-drug conjugate and checkpoint blockade combinations for triple-negative breast cancer.
title: Counting immune cells in a tumor tells you less than whether they survive there
blurb: A review arguing that ADC plus checkpoint blockade trials in triple-negative breast cancer keep measuring immune-cell abundance when what predicts outcome is whether those cells actually persist inside the tumor. Fate over headcount, and current trial endpoints mostly aren't set up to catch that.

original_title: Linking vibrational energetics to carbon isotope separation in CO<sub>2</sub> electrolysis
title: Why CO2 electrolysis enriches carbon-13 the way it does
blurb: Nature Chemistry ties the vibrational energetics of CO2 reduction directly to how much 13C gets enriched, giving carbon isotope separation something it's lacked: a link from catalyst design to isotopologue outcome you could actually predict instead of just stumbling into.

original_title: Photocatalytic Phosphine‐mediated Hydroxymethylation of Alkenes With Formaldehyde Hydrate
title: Formaldehyde water finally gives up a clean hydroxymethyl radical
blurb: Visible light kicks a phosphine to its radical cation, which grabs formaldehyde hydrate and releases a hydroxymethyl radical by beta-scission, no protecting groups needed. That radical adds regioselectively across electron-poor alkenes, turning a notoriously messy C1 feedstock into a usable hydroxymethylation handle.

original_title: Computational Analysis of Competing Reduction Pathways in the Asymmetric Transfer Hydrogenation of 2-Alkenylquinolines
title: Two different hydride transfers, same enantiomer either way
blurb: Computations on asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of 2-alkenylquinolines find two nearly isoenergetic first-step pathways, hydride landing on the quinoline ring or the alkenyl chain, that both funnel into the same prochiral iminium. The chiral phosphoric acid only has to control the final 1,2-hydride step, which is why the stereochemistry comes out consistent even though the mechanism apparently isn't.

original_title: Topological Integration of Slide‐Ring and Entangled Networks
title: Slide-rings and entanglements finally sharing one elastomer network
blurb: Slide-ring networks and entangled networks each toughen elastomers through their own trick, mobile crosslinks versus physical interlocking, and this builds both into a single network to see if the two effects stack rather than just coexist.

original_title: From Photoswitch to Polycycle: Structure–Reactivity Relationships in the Photoinduced Isomerization–Cyclization of Amino(hetero)arylidene‐thiazolidine‐2,4‐diones
title: What makes these photoswitches actually cyclize instead of just flip
blurb: A TD-DFT-guided study of amino(hetero)arylidene-thiazolidinediones maps how substitution pattern controls whether photoisomerization cascades on into a full cyclization. Position 4 on the aromatic ring turns out to be the lever, and that prediction held up across a broad library they built to test it, heteroaryl versions included.

original_title: Nascent Extracellular Matrix Converts Biomaterial Cues into Cell Fate Decisions
title: The matrix cells lay down themselves outranks the one you engineer
blurb: Cells sitting on a chemically modified hydrogel quietly deposit their own nascent ECM at the interface, and it's that self-made layer, not the hydrogel's chemistry directly, that ends up dictating cell fate. So tuning a hydrogel's chemical modifications may be doing less than everyone assumes, and the nascent ECM is doing the actual interpreting.

original_title: Realization of a Manufacturing‐Scale Synthesis of Niraparib Using an Evolved Transaminase
title: Getting a PARP inhibitor's enzyme to work at plant scale
blurb: Nine rounds of directed evolution on a transaminase, paired with pushing the substrate concentration harder, turned a biocatalytic step for niraparib into something that actually runs at manufacturing scale rather than just in a flask. The unglamorous part of biocatalysis, scale-up, is the whole point here.

original_title: Triadic σ–π Coordination Programs Cuδ+ Sites to Drive Sequential Dual-N Species C–N Coupling for Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis
title: Tuning what sits next to the Cu atom to make urea from CO2 and nitrate
blurb: Electrochemical CO2/nitrate coupling to urea usually stalls because the carbon- and nitrogen-derived intermediates don't show up at the active site in sync, and they crowd or repel each other when they do. Here the fix is second-sphere coordination: single-atom Cu-alkynyl-X sites in conjugated microporous polymers, with X swapped between N, C, and S, so the σ→Cu donation programs the copper's charge state and stages the two intermediates for coupling in sequence instead of letting them fight for the same spot.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Optimizing CRBN-ligands for optical targeted protein degradation.
title: Better CRBN handles for light-controlled protein degraders
blurb: Optimizing the CRBN-binding ligand used in optically triggered targeted protein degradation, the piece that decides whether the degrader actually switches on and off with light. Thin on details beyond that, but it's the medicinal chemistry side of making photo-controlled PROTACs work better.

original_title: Catalyst design in heterogeneous deuteration: recent advances and perspectives
title: A review of catalysts for cheap, recoverable deuteration
blurb: A survey of heterogeneous catalytic strategies that use D2O instead of pricier deuterium sources, and skip the noble metals that are hard to recover afterward. The pitch across the field is catalyst reuse and simpler workups, not any single flashy result.

original_title: Molecular-Level Cleavage and Kinetics Optimization in PVDF Electrolytes for Anode-Lean Ultrastable Solid-State Sodium Batteries
title: Na3P eats its own electrolyte's C–F bonds on purpose
blurb: A PVDF solid electrolyte for sodium batteries where Na3P isn't just a filler, its nucleophilic P3- deliberately cleaves C–F bonds, cutting polymer crystallinity and releasing F- while the Na3P itself doubles as a fast ion conductor. Simulations show it also reshapes the solvation structure and lowers the desolvation barrier, the combination aimed at anode-lean, ultrastable solid-state Na cells.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli
title: Getting a tungsten enzyme to fold in E. coli with the lights on
blurb: Tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases are some of the best CO2-reduction catalysts known, but they usually need anaerobic conditions and cofactor machinery standard hosts don't have. Rebuilding the tungsten-cofactor pathway, adding a high-affinity tungstate transporter, and reinforcing iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis lets E. coli produce the M. extorquens enzyme aerobically at native-level activity.

original_title: Synthesis, Conformation, and Pro‐Inflammatory Activity of the Branched Glucorhamnans Relevant to the Polysaccharide of Ruminococcus gnavus
title: Synthesizing the gut-bacterial sugar tied to Crohn's inflammation
blurb: Branched glucorhamnan fragments matching the R. gnavus polysaccharide implicated in Crohn's disease, built by solving the 1,2-trans glycosidic linkages that make this backbone a pain to assemble. The point of having clean synthetic fragments is finally being able to test what in the structure actually drives the inflammatory response, with a carbohydrate vaccine as the longer-term angle.

original_title: Influence of Central Metal and Halide Size on the Structure and Photophysics of Group 4 Arylalkynyl Metallocenes and their CuX (X = Cl, Br, I) Complexes
title: Swap Zr for Ti in these alkynyl metallocenes and the emission shifts
blurb: A structure-photophysics comparison across group 4 arylalkynyl metallocenes and their CuX-bridged (Cl, Br, I) versions. The zirconium complex is isostructural with its titanium twin by X-ray, but blue-shifts its emission at 77 K, a clean case of the same scaffold behaving differently once you change the metal.

original_title: Indium–Oxygen Integrative Catalytic Pairs for Boosting Asymmetric C–C Coupling in Electrochemical Formic Acid Reduction Reaction
title: In-O pairs push formic acid reduction past the usual C1 stop
blurb: A theory-guided hunt turns up indium-oxygen catalytic pairs on carbon support that drive asymmetric C-C coupling during electrochemical formic acid reduction, aiming at acetaldehyde and ethanol instead of the more common single-carbon products. Constant-potential DFT and AIMD point to the In-O sites' structural flexibility as what makes the coupling possible.

original_title: The TROP2 targeting antibody-drug conjugate IMMU-132 enhances the efficacy of radiation therapy for lung cancer
title: Sacituzumab govitecan isn't approved for lung cancer, so they paired it with radiation anyway
blurb: TROP2 is overexpressed in most lung cancers, but the TROP2 ADC sacituzumab govitecan (IMMU-132) is currently only approved for breast and bladder cancer. Combined with radiation it boosted efficacy against NSCLC in both cell culture and animal models, a preclinical case for repurposing an already-approved ADC rather than waiting on a new one.

original_title: H/F Substitution Regulates the Local Environment and Excited-State Relaxation of Tetrahedral Mn(II) Centers for Near-Unity Luminescence and X-ray Scintillation
title: One H-to-F swap nearly doubles a manganese scintillator's brightness
blurb: Replacing H with F on the organic cation in a zero-dimensional Mn(II) hybrid chloride introduces F···Cl interactions that subtly reshape the MnCl4 coordination environment, and that alone takes the photoluminescence quantum yield from 49.8% to near-unity. The payoff is a brighter, more efficient X-ray scintillator from a fairly small structural tweak.

original_title: On‐Surface Friedel–Crafts Alkylation Through a Stabilized Intermediate Complex
title: Friedel-Crafts alkylation, but the surface is the catalyst
blurb: An intramolecular C-C coupling run directly on a metal surface, using a purpose-built fluorinated aromatic reactant so the substrate and catalyst are effectively the same molecule. On-surface C-C bond formation is still rare next to the well-worn coupling chemistries, so getting an sp3 center into a planar carbon nanostructure this way is the actual news.

original_title: Structural basis of stepwise G protein activation by the viral chemokine receptor US28
title: Catching a GPCR mid-handshake with its G protein
blurb: Cryo-EM on the viral chemokine receptor US28 bound to Gq, using an engineered superagonist to freeze three separate steps: GDP still bound, nucleotide gone, and a transition state bridging the two. First time the activation sequence has been pulled apart structurally instead of guessed at from the endpoints.

original_title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Glycosylation of Styrenes with Glycosyl Acids and Pyridines via Decarboxylation
title: A three-way glycosylation that skips the usual two-partner limit
blurb: Visible light drives a decarboxylative coupling of glycosyl acids, styrenes, and cyanopyridines into C-glycosides in one pot through a glycosyl radical pathway. Tolerates a wide range of styrenes and protected sugars, reaches into pharma fragments, and scales to grams, which most glycosylation methods can't claim.

original_title: Regioselective C‐H Oxyfunctionalization of Aliphatic Acids Through a Consecutive Biosolar Cascade
title: Sunlight and a P450 enzyme team up to oxidize fatty acids
blurb: A sodium-potassium-doped carbon nitride photocatalyst feeds electrons into a two-electron oxygen reduction under visible light, and that feeds a cytochrome P450 peroxygenase doing regioselective C-H oxidation on aliphatic acids. The alkali doping is there to juice the photocatalyst's surface field so it can actually keep the enzyme supplied.

original_title: Design of Experiments for Diverse Carbon Isotope Labeling with Aryl Thianthrenium Salts
title: Carbon-isotope labeling of aryl thianthrenium salts, DoE-optimized
blurb: Near-stoichiometric ex situ CO plus plain air-stable Pd catalysts turns aryl thianthrenium salts into a broad set of carbon-isotope-labeled carbonylation products, with Design of Experiments doing the optimization and mechanistic digging. The scope reaches late-stage labeling of actual pharmaceutical molecules, not just model substrates.

original_title: Enantioselective Formal Synthesis of (−)-Neoxaline Enabled by an Asymmetric Ir-Catalyzed Reverse Prenylation
title: A shorter route to neoxaline via reverse prenylation
blurb: A formal synthesis of the alkaloid neoxaline built around asymmetric Ir-catalyzed reverse prenylation onto a tryptamine scaffold to assemble its dense α-carboline core, after an earlier attempt used deaminative cross-coupling onto oxindole instead. Pitched as a general strategy for the rest of the oxaline alkaloids, not just this one target.

original_title: An Internal-Standard-Integrated Digital SERS Immunoassay for Accurate and Precise Trace-Level Cytokine Quantification in Plasma
title: A SERS immunoassay that corrects its own drift
blurb: A digital SERS platform for IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12, and TNF-α that adds an orthogonal recombinant protein as an internal standard to cancel out assay- and instrument-level noise, pushing quantification down to attomolar levels in plasma. That internal standard is the actual fix: cytokines have been too noisy in complex matrices to trust as longitudinal biomarkers.

original_title: Self-Transforming Antibiofilm Polyurethane Copolymers with Arginine-Mimetic Cationic Activity for Infection-Resistant Implants
title: Polyurethane implant coatings that fight biofilm with arginine mimicry
blurb: Antibiofilm polyurethane copolymers carrying arginine-mimetic cationic groups, designed to self-transform, aimed at infection-resistant implants. No performance numbers to go on, just the design.

original_title: Designing Porous Boroaluminate Catalysts via Non‐Hydrolytic Ether Elimination
title: Boroaluminate xerogels made without water
blurb: A non-hydrolytic sol-gel route builds porous boroaluminate catalysts through ether elimination instead of the usual hydrolysis, run across four combinations of aluminum and boron alkoxide precursors. Template-free and mildly acidic is the pitch, but it's still precursor-screening stage.
venue: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

original_title: Bridging the PSMA PET/CT access gap in prostate cancer: evidence, barriers, and priorities for implementation.
title: PSMA PET/CT works great, if you can actually get one
blurb: A review laying out the evidence for PSMA PET/CT in prostate cancer, the practical barriers keeping access uneven, and where implementation efforts should focus next. No new data, just the gap and what to do about it.

original_title: Recent Progress in PET and SPECT Myocardial Perfusion Imaging: From Radiopharmaceuticals to Imaging Innovations.
title: A tour of PET and SPECT tracers for imaging heart blood flow
blurb: A review rounding up where myocardial perfusion imaging stands, from the radiopharmaceuticals themselves to the scanner-side advances used to read them. No new data, just a snapshot of the field.

original_title: MTTI wins $3.2M NCI grant to develop lung cancer radiopharmaceutical - Dealroom
title: NCI hands MTTI $3.2M to chase a lung cancer radiopharmaceutical
blurb: A grant, not a result: $3.2M from NCI to fund development of a lung cancer radiopharmaceutical. Worth another look once there's actual data behind it.

original_title: An Injectable Polyurethane/Hyaluronic Acid Hybrid Hydrogel for Glucose-Responsive CAPE Release and Immune Remodeling in Diabetic Wound Healing.
title: A wound dressing that senses glucose and doles out CAPE accordingly
blurb: An injectable hydrogel built from polyurethane and hyaluronic acid that releases caffeic acid phenethyl ester in response to glucose levels, and remodels the local immune response, aimed at diabetic wounds. Glucose-responsive release makes sense here specifically because the sugar swings are the whole problem.

original_title: Instantaneous Mechanical Programming of Polymer Microparticle Shape and Surface Architecture
title: Turning spherical particles into cylinders with nothing but rubbing
blurb: A rubbing process that reshapes spherical polymer microparticles into cylinders and textures their surfaces in one mechanical pass, by tuning plasticization, pressure, and stress transmission rather than running a multi-step fabrication process. Quick way to get anisotropic particles without the usual lithography fuss.

original_title: Cell-derived lactate triggers local hydrogelation and phenotype remodelling.
title: Lactate leaking out of cells sets off gelation nearby
blurb: Lactate released by cells is enough on its own to trigger local hydrogel formation and shift the phenotype of nearby cells, per this Nat Commun paper. A metabolite acting as its own construction signal, if it holds up outside this system.

original_title: Microwave-assisted extraction enhances wet-heating Maillard glycation of lupin protein with galacto-oligosaccharides: structural basis for improved interfacial functionality and gut fermentability
title: Microwaving lupin protein first makes the later glycation work better
blurb: Microwave-assisted extraction of lupin protein isolate, done before any glycation, sets it up for a better wet-heat Maillard reaction with galacto-oligosaccharides: degree of grafting hits 22% and particle size drops down from around 17, with partial unfolding that improves interfacial behavior and gut fermentability. So the extraction step is doing real conditioning work, not just recovering the protein.

original_title: Enhanced 3D Osteogenic Differentiation of Encapsulated Human MSCs in Hyaluronic Acid Core Alginate Shell Capsules under Dynamic Culture Conditions
title: Core-shell capsules give MSCs a better shot at becoming bone in 3D
blurb: Human mesenchymal stem cells encapsulated in hyaluronic acid core, alginate shell capsules show enhanced osteogenic differentiation under dynamic culture. The point is a 3D model that doesn't force cells flat onto a dish to study bone formation.

original_title: DNA-Peptide Nanoassembly for Mitochondria-Specific and Programmable Subcellular Apoptotic Regulation.
title: A DNA-peptide nanoassembly that dials mitochondrial apoptosis up or down
blurb: A DNA-peptide nanoassembly engineered to home in on mitochondria and give programmable, subcellular control over apoptosis. Light on mechanism detail here, but mitochondria-targeted control over cell death is a genuinely useful knob to have.
